title: Wrong Object Paths
summary: The object exists — just not where your code looks. Misplaced services, renamed objects, wrong containers (workspace vs ReplicatedStorage), and dot-paths that don't match Explorer reality all produce nils.

explanation.whatItIs: The treasure map disagrees with the terrain: the name is right, the address isn't.
explanation.whyItExists: Paths are strings in disguise; moving/renaming anything in Explorer invalidates them silently.
symptoms: FindFirstChild returns nil but you can SEE it in Explorer
GetService vs dot access mismatch on services
explanation.fix: Print the full path from Explorer (right-click → Copy Full Path), compare hop by hop; prefer GetService for services; WaitForChild for async containers.
tips: game:GetService("X") beats game.X for services (case-safe, exists-safe)
Centralize paths in one module so renames touch one place
Use CollectionService tags for 'find all the traps' instead of remembering folders
commonMistakes: workspace.MyPart vs Workspace.MyPart confusion after moving containers
Looking in ReplicatedStorage for something that's in ServerStorage
Hardcoded paths into temporary objects (characters, tools)

examples.title: Path debugging
examples.code:
-- You believe it's here:
local part = workspace.Map:FindFirstChild("Key")

-- But maybe it's actually:
-- ReplicatedStorage.Items.Key  (moved during a refactor!)

-- Debug helper:
local function where(name)
    for _, obj in workspace:GetDescendants() do
        if obj.Name == name then
            print("Found at:", obj:GetFullName())
        end
    end
end
where("Key")
